newEntities.label: Bacterial curli/DNA
newEntities.description: Purified bacterial biofilm curli/DNA exposure studied as an upstream autoantibody stimulus in mice; not an established cause of human SLE.

findings.subject: entity-curli-dna
findings.studySystem: Purified biofilm curli/DNA exposure in C57BL/6, NZBxW/F1 and MRL/lpr mice; Salmonella infection in wild-type mice. No human intervention.
findings.text: Purified bacterial curli/DNA exposure increased anti-C1q autoantibodies in wild-type and lupus-prone mice; anti-dsDNA responses also increased in young NZBxW/F1 mice. Effects depended on model and disease stage.
findings.quote: An anti-C1q-specific ELISA confirmed the presence of anti-C1q antibodies in C57BL/6 mice after treatment with curli/DNA, extracted from E. coli or Salmonella biofilms, or infection with Salmonella.
findings.quoteLocation: Publisher Abstract; Results: Curli treatment or infection with STm induces anti-C1q autoantibodies; figures 1, 3 and 4.
limitations: Purified material was administered intraperitoneally; infection experiments are separate and do not establish a human gut-to-SLE pathway.
The Luminex C57BL/6 comparison was not significant, whereas separate anti-C1q ELISA experiments supported induction.
Proteinuria, kidney pathology and circulating C1q did not differ significantly at the measured timepoints; increased autoantibodies or glomerular C1q deposition do not establish worsened nephritis.

findings.subject: entity-curli-dna
findings.studySystem: Purified biofilm curli/DNA exposure in C57BL/6, NZBxW/F1 and MRL/lpr mice; Salmonella infection in wild-type mice. No human intervention.
findings.text: Curli did not further increase already-high autoantibody responses in late-disease NZBxW/F1 mice; the study also found no significant proteinuria increase in either lupus-prone model, limiting translation from autoantibody induction to renal disease.
findings.quote: however, no differences were found in older mice, post-onset, when autoantibody levels were already high.
findings.quoteLocation: Publisher Abstract; Results: Curli induces anti-C1q autoantibodies in NZBxW/F1 mice (figure 3); renal function results and figure 5.
limitations: A null difference at selected ages and timepoints does not prove absence of an effect at later stages or in humans.
MRL/lpr mice retained an anti-C1q response; the stage limit is not uniform across models.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Separate negative disease-stage and renal outcome findings qualify the positive induction result from the same experiment series.
